items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So I go over there, and we’re sitting in the lounge of the Inn itself, and Miles and them show up. I think Miles came and he split, but Kenny Dennis stayed, and Bill Evans stayed.

ctx.x: Don Jacobi. So when we went to Lenox, and then he – George came out to Indianapolis, we started the sextet in all earnestness. George rehearsed us every day. We were already playing every night. He turned it into the George Russell Sextet. When we became the George Russell Sextet, George then took us to New York. We opened at the Five Spot opposite a group of – that had Jim Hall, Billy Osborne on drums, Jimmy Giuffre on saxophone, and Buell Neidlinger on bass. We played any number of weeks opposite that group at…
Maybe we should break for just a second.
